motions.title: Adopt a multi-store recall architecture: fabric + structured SQL + ChEMBL co-processor
motions.description: The platform's knowledge is THREE tiers, not one: (1) the main fabric -- 2,180 documents (124 papers + 1,994 relational records + 62 markdown) encoded as .k3 trits + 2-bit turbovec + sidecar; (2) the structured SQL store -- ~3.9M rows across 10 tables (molecule 2.9M ChEMBL, tox21 578K, clinical 201K, ethics 96K, binding 19K, prose 1.6K); (3) the ChEMBL co-processor fabric -- 2,897,805 compounds (2-bit turbovec + K3 ternary + sidecar, just completed). The relational tier's 1,994 sidecar stubs were empty ('source is not a file on disk') and are now fixed to carry real text (sidecar real-text records 180 -> 2,174; sha256 verified). Recall must route a query BY KIND -- general/prose -> fabric_recall, molecule/semantic -> ChEMBL co-processor, structured fact -> SQL -- rather than dumping everything into one index. A single fabric_recall over ChEMBL would have replaced the 2,180-doc sovereign knowledge base with one molecule domain; that framing is rejected.

motions.title: Split on-device vs host-side stores; ChEMBL + fabric on-device, SQL host-side
motions.description: On-device recall (the boot volume) should carry the fabric (2,180 docs, ~77 MB .k3 + ~2 MB sidecar + turbovec family) plus the ChEMBL co-processor (turbovec 648 MB + ternary 625 MB + sidecar 810 MB = ~2.1 GB). The structured SQL store (~3.9M rows) is a structured-query surface (filters, joins, property lookups), not a semantic-recall store, and is best served host-side from structured_index.db. The 2.1 GB ChEMBL fabric must be confirmed to fit the boot volume before it is copied on-device -- a size check, not an assumption.
